messages.subject: Milkweed seeds
messages.text:
I bought some milkweed seeds this spring and received them a couple of weeks ago. I just looked at the planting instructions and it says the seeds need to be stratified before planting. If I stratify them for 30 days now, won't it be too late to plant them?
 Were these seeds in cold storage over the winter? Or should I put them in the freezer and plant in the fall?

 
Thanks for any input,

 
Pixie Senesac

 
Trumansburg NY

messages.subject: Re: Milkweed seeds
messages.text:
Hi Pixie,

Sorry for the long wait on this, things have been really intense on our end and this took far longer than it should have. We'll do better.

To your questions: the seeds you bought are the regular (non-stratified) ones, so they do need that cold-moist period before spring planting. If you stratify now and plant in August, it would likely be a bit late for strong germination this season.

Here are your two best options:

1. Fall planting (easiest and most reliable): put the seeds directly in the ground this fall, before it freezes. Winter takes care of the stratification naturally, and they should come up in spring.

2. Stratify now (about 30 days in the fridge, in a slightly moist paper towel inside a bag), then plant. It's tight this late in the season, but doable if your growing season runs long enough.

Either way works, so I'd lean toward the fall planting if you'd rather keep it simple. No need to put them in the freezer.

Our planting guide has more detail if it helps: https://lasclay.com/en/pages/planting-guide

If anything comes up as you go, just let me know.

Warmly,
__
 Gabriel Gouveia 
Co-founder
Lasclay.com
